what: The closed grammar for an announced account value, as BOTH stacks must read it.
why: CON-005 says a malformed value is treated as absent, which makes disagreement between implementations invisible: one stack renders attribution and the other renders an unmarked member, and neither reports an error. A shared vector file is the only way that divergence shows up as a failing test rather than as two clients disagreeing about who somebody is. This is the same device successor-pointer-vector.json uses for REQ-039.
authority: apps/cbcl_chat/priv/web/announce-did.mjs — the browser recogniser. A second stack agrees with it or the vector fails there.

accept.why: the canonical form: lowercase hex, exactly 64 characters
every hex digit appears; nothing about the alphabet is positional
the upper bound of the digest space is not a special case

reject.why: uppercase hex — one account MUST NOT have two spellings, or a pin keyed on the string forks
mixed case, for the same reason; a case-folding reader would accept it and key on a different string
63 characters — a truncated digest is not a shorter account, it is a different one
outside the hex alphabet, at the right length
the scheme is matched literally, not case-insensitively as RFC 3986 would allow — this is a wire token, not a URI to dereference
a trailing space — the anchor is the point, and a reader that trims would accept a value the other stack rejects
a trailing newline — a line-oriented reader is the likeliest way a second stack diverges here
another DID method at the right shape — CON-005 admits exactly one
